title: Derived isomorphism for the fixed local relative tensor complex
statement: Let f:X→S be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], E an object of D(O_X) [def-pc-derived-category], and G,K cochain complexes of O_X-modules. Fix eK:QK≅E tensor-derived QG [def-pc-scheme-derived-tensor-structure]. Let U be an open subset, L a strictly perfect complex of O_X|_U-modules [def-pc-perfect-complex], and eL:E|_U≅QL. Put R=f inverse-image O_S and let A be its underlying ring sheaf. In the standard localization of complexes of A|_U-modules at quasi-isomorphisms [def-pc-quasi-iso-modules], the localization of (scalar restriction of K along R→O_X)|_U is isomorphic to the localization of strictPerfectRelativeTensorComplex f U L G [def-pc-strict-perfect-relative-tensor-complex]. This asserts only the local derived comparison, not the existence of a common complex or chain-map roof.

source.place: Tag 0DJQ, proof, local strict-perfect tensor calculation; Tag 06YH, derived tensor construction after K-flat resolutions; original roof node proof step 1 and the scalar-restriction part of step 2

proof.text: Finite-free retract terms of the bounded complex L are structure-ring flat; bounded-above flat complexes are K-flat. Restrict eK using exact monoidal open restriction, substitute eL for the first factor, and apply K-flat derived tensor comparison. Transport between the localized site and the open subscheme by the module equivalence to get the derived isomorphism from K|_U to the ordinary total tensor L tensor G|_U.

Restriction of scalars along the base-ring map is exact: on the underlying sheaf of abelian groups it changes neither sections nor differentials, so it preserves cohomology. It therefore descends to the localizations at quasi-isomorphisms. Apply this functor to the local derived tensor comparison from the previous step. Open restriction and scalar restriction commute sectionwise, identifying its first endpoint with the displayed scalar-restricted K. By definition its second endpoint is the explicit relative tensor complex. Use the standard localization for A|_U, whose hom universe is u+1; no base-ring localization hypothesis is necessary.

theorem strictPerfect_relativeTensor_roof_comparison
    {X S : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S)
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace))]
    [∀ U : X.Opens,
      HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over U))]
    (E : schemeDerivedCategory X)
    (G K : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)) ℤ)
    (eK : DerivedCategory.Q.obj K ≅ E ⊗ DerivedCategory.Q.obj G)
    (U : X.Opens)
    (L : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over U)) ℤ)
    (hL : IsStrictlyPerfect X U L)
    (eL : (SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{u}
      (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace) U).mapDerivedCategory.obj E ≅ DerivedCategory.Q.obj L) :
    let R := TopCat.Sheaf.inverseImageRing f.base S.sheaf
    let A := (sheafCompose (Opens.grothendieckTopology X)
      (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u})).obj R
    letI : HasDerivedCategory.{u + 1} (SheafOfModules.{u} (A.over U)) :=
      HasDerivedCategory.standard _
    Nonempty
      (DerivedCategory.Q.obj
        (((SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{u} A U).mapHomologicalComplex
          (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj
          (((SheafOfModules.restrictScalars
            ((sheafCompose (Opens.grothendieckTopology X)
              (forget₂ CommRingCat.{u} RingCat.{u})).map
                (Modules.tensorPullbackRingMap f))).mapHomologicalComplex
            (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj K)) ≅
        DerivedCategory.Q.obj (strictPerfectRelativeTensorComplex f U L G))
